name: ffmpeg-normalize
notes: 2026-11-01: EBU R128 two-pass loudness normalisation CLI with presets and batch mode.
2026-11-15: Release page identifies 1.43.0 (2026-10-14) as latest; current repository pyproject reports 1.44.0. Release tag/date for 1.44.0 not confirmed.
2026-11-24: Toolkit guide written from ffmpeg-normalize-loudness evidence (linear two-pass, sine bursts only); documents the silent loudnorm dynamic fallback and explicit -ar.

evidence.result: Two generated 10 s 48 kHz stereo sine-burst WAVs (input -29.1 and -10.7 LUFS, LRA 1.8 LU each) normalised with -nt ebu -t -16 -tp -1.5 -ar 48000: outputs -16.1 LUFS each (tolerance 0.5 LU), true peak -11.4 dBTP each (ceiling -1.5), LRA unchanged, duration 10.000 s, 48000 Hz, rerun PCM MD5 identical. Default options also gave 48000 Hz. Linear gain used (no loudnorm revert). FFmpeg 9.0.2 ebur128 measurement.
evidence.scope: EBU R128 linear normalisation to -16 LUFS, -1.5 dBTP; sine bursts only, ceiling never binding; 48 kHz kept; macOS arm64, FFmpeg 9.0.2

summary: Python CLI and API built on FFmpeg for batch EBU R128, RMS or peak loudness normalisation. It can preserve video streams and selectively process audio tracks; output is re-encoded media with configurable codecs and metadata. Its distinguishing strength is album-style batch normalisation that preserves relative levels.
use_when: Normalise audio loudness in batches with EBU R128, RMS or peak targets
Over raw FFmpeg filters when batch handling and preset reuse matter
avoid_when: Use FFmpeg directly for custom filtergraphs or when only measuring loudness
Use a DAW when manual mix decisions or mastering are required

install.macos: uv tool install ffmpeg-normalize (requires Python >=3.10 and FFmpeg)

assessment.rationale: The release page lists v1.43.0 (2026-10-14), while current main pyproject reports 1.44.0; MIT and active development. Batch R128/RMS/peak normalization adds a focused audio workflow beyond FFmpeg itself.
